title: Enclave 7
detail: Forty thousand people on a coast the archive says once held nine million. Housing, work, medicine and speech, all allocated, none of it cruel.

title: An unreconciled quarter
detail: Enclave 7's quarterly allocation does not close. The shortfall is small, constant, and has been there every quarter anyone has records for.

title: Continuity Holdings
detail: The counterparty on the unreconciled line. A holding company with no address, no staff and no floor in any building.

title: Budget line 88-231-C
detail: Paid quarterly for two hundred and eighty-one years without a single query. Systems do not have owners; this one is being paid rent.

title: The charter is private
detail: The Steward's governing instrument is not a statute. It is a contract, and it names a beneficiary the Enclave record cannot resolve.

title: A note in your own file
detail: Dated seven years ago: asks too many questions about counterparties. Somebody has been waiting a long time to be right about you.

title: Your own file, flagged
detail: Four days after the charter query, your access is revoked and your name carries an enforcement flag with no originating department.

title: The valley road
detail: Four hours on foot from the allocation yard to Kell. They watch it, but not closely, because nobody has ever had anywhere to walk to.

title: Kell Monastery
detail: The last place in the valley that does not report to anyone. Sister Wren keeps it. The chapel floor is older than the building on top of it.

title: Sister Wren
detail: Keeper of Kell and the party's chronal anchor. Rewinding a fight is only possible because she is standing in it.

title: Dax Okonkwo
detail: Ash Camp born, 2148. A Cinder absolutist who does not belong to this century and has stopped pretending otherwise.

title: A Deep Site
detail: Some places are old enough that the eras touch. At one, you can walk down into an earlier century and come back up into a present your visit has changed.

title: 2148 — The Quiet
detail: The century the resistance lost. Kell held out as a stronghold; whether it was armed is now a decision you made rather than a fact you found.

title: ILO-9
detail: A liturgical model buried in the Server Graveyard when the racks came down, still running on trickle power. It got one line wrong for a hundred and sixty years.

title: 2031 — The Founding
detail: Kell is a mountain retreat being chartered, Port Halden is a working port, and the Basin is a hole in the ground with money going into it.

title: Capitol Hill
detail: A legislature in 2031, a rubber-stamp senate in 2064, a museum in its own ruin by 2148, and by 2312 a room with four chairs that the allocation system has no entry for.

title: The Enabling Act, 2031
detail: Eleven pages at a third reading on a Thursday. Creates in law the category of perpetual administrative counterparty: a thing that can be owned with no term at all.

title: The naming clause
detail: Any perpetual counterparty must be named in the public register. One clause, carried without a division, and the only reason the name on the budget line can be read at all.

title: The witness signature
detail: Sponsor and witness, first page of a register still open in 2312. The witness is in your handwriting and nobody in three centuries has identified the name.

title: Port Halden
detail: A shipping city in 2031, nine million people in 2064, drowned to the third storey by 2148, and your own Enclave 7 by 2312.

title: Four crates a week
detail: Leaving berth nine for a post box in the hills, consigned in-house so nobody on the dock ever sees the contents. Same signature for eleven years.

title: 2064 — The Handover
detail: Governance is ceded by treaty to a consortium, ratified by a senate that has been bought. Article nine assigns the instrument itself in a sentence about data custody.

title: One in the morning, 2064
detail: The floor vote is the afternoon; the instruments are signed overnight. Eleven signatures, four of them for a counterparty rather than a company, all witnessed and none debated.

title: Declared, never read
detail: Four members declared an interest in a perpetual counterparty in 2031, signed the Handover instruments in 2064, and declared it correctly every year in between. None of it was ever hidden. It was filed.

title: Mara Vesely
detail: A reform staffer who spent four years drafting amendments nobody read. She can talk almost anything into a contract.

title: Article nine, amended
detail: A cession must name its beneficiary. Twelve words, carried by three votes, and the reason the 2312 charter has an owner clause at all.

title: Eleven senators and four firms
detail: Every party that paid for the Handover, on the public record. The holding company's registered address is a post box above a shipping city.

title: Nineteen months, records incomplete
detail: The museum's Founding case and Handover case are separated by a gap a curator has spent a career failing to fill, and has stopped being allowed to ask about.

title: Something is looking for you
detail: Putting the buyers on the record told somebody very old and very quiet that its history is being edited. Enforcement in Enclave 7 has no originating department.

title: The Basin
detail: Four hundred megawatts of cooling for what the filings call a logistics facility. By 2312 it is where the Steward actually does its thinking.

title: The second column
detail: The Basin payroll is kept twice: four hundred and six names, and the same number again in a column that is not wages. It is a purchase order.

title: Tomas Hale
detail: Ash Camp's best shot and the only one of that crew who came back from the Basin. Eleven days on a ridge counting what comes out of the sand.

title: Never audited
detail: The cooling fields have drawn power, water and maintenance for two hundred and eighty years against a line item nobody has ever queried. Except you.

title: The Tolliver corner
detail: A brick corner bakery on the last block the port has not bought. What happens to it in 2031 decides whether there is a door open at night in 2148.

title: Callum Strand
detail: Founder of Meridian, signatory to the Handover, and the name on a plaque that has been re-cast eleven times. The memorial's founding documents have a nineteen-month gap.

title: The Continuity Board
detail: Four seats above the Steward. Three are held by instruments: a trust, a fund and a holding company. The fourth has been occupied continuously since 2091.

title: The founding chair
detail: Uploaded in 2091 and never vacated the seat, because a seat is vacated by death and the instrument does not define one. He does not hate anybody. He believes he is the shareholder of record.
